messages:
alex: quick sync — follow-up on tenant QoS + evictor preemption. after the last perf run we saw tenant A's background compaction destroy tenant B's p99. need a practical strategy to enforce tenant-level fairness in the async-evictor.

maria: ugh. do we have telemetry confirming compaction is the culprit or just eviction churn?

ben: traces show long compaction CPU bursts coinciding with spikes. eviction itself was ok, but compactor pinned cores for ~800ms which delayed inference threads.

chris: two orthogonal knobs: 1) admission: rate-limit compaction tasks per-tenant; 2) preemption: evictor should be able to demote a compaction into low-prio work if system is overloaded.

sara: agree. propose `evict_priority` levels (critical, regular, background). default eviction requests from inference path map to critical. compaction tasks are regular/background.

rachel: how do we surface that to allocator API? callers shouldn't have to know about compaction. maybe allocator returns a hint header like `Evict-Admitted: critical|regular|backoff` when request accepted or throttled.

alex: sketch API:
```
// returns admission token + granted priority
EvictAdmission admit_eviction(RangeId r, int pages, Priority pref);
// EvictAdmission = { token_id, granted_priority, ttl_s }
```
If granted_priority < pref caller can reduce batch size or fallback.

maria: TTL on admission is good to avoid stale tokens. also need an admin path to bump a tenant's quota for troubleshooting.

chris: runtime should enforce global invariants: cap on concurrent critical compactions per-node, per-tenant compaction budget, and a global background budget for opportunistic defrag. these are additive checks in the admission path.

ben: what about preemption semantics? if compactors are running and a critical evict arrives, can we interrupt and preempt some background compactions? preemption has costs (rollbacks) but might be necessary for SLAs.

sara: introduce cooperative preemption: compaction tasks poll a `should_yield()` flag and break workpoints frequently. preemption granularity tuned to avoid huge rollback cost. also rank tasks by tenant priority when yielding.

rachel: for Private customers we might allow stronger preemption (sync shrink on request). we should expose `tenant_profile` config: {priority, compaction_budget, allow_sync_shrink}.

alex: telemetry items: `compaction_cpu_ms_by_tenant`, `compaction_yields`, `evict_admit_rate`, `evict_denied_reasons` (quota, queue, fragmentation), `preempt_count`. will add alert when compaction_cpu_ms / node > threshold.

chris: failure modes: admitted token might expire before evictor runs -> eviction fails gracefully and caller receives `ERR_EVICT_TOKEN_EXPIRED`. SDKs should gracefully degrade.

ben: SDK behavior: on `ERR_EVICT_TOKEN_EXPIRED` or `ERR_EVICTOR_OVERLOADED` callers retry once after reducing batch size by 30% and set `X-Evict-Retry: 1`. add server-side guidance header `Retry-Backoff: 50ms`.

maria: also add a soft SLA: critical admissions should be fulfilled within `admit_timeout` ms or returned as refused. we can tune `admit_timeout` per deployment class.

alex: operational knobs: `--compaction-cpu-quota-per-tenant`, `--max-critical-compactions`, `--evict-admit-window-ms`. default conservative. for Dedicated customers we expose a tenant-config API to increase budgets.

sara: testing plan: synthetic load that runs mixed tenants with adversarial compaction to validate fairness. also a chaos test that randomly flaps compaction budgets.

rachel: follow-up: do we need eviction preflight that checks fragmentation and suggests `force_compact`? maybe `admit_eviction` returns `fragmentation_hint` bucket: {low, medium, high}. caller could opt to call admin `force_compact` if high and has quota.

chris: careful — exposing fragmentation hints to product code could encourage bad behavior. prefer runtime to automatically escalate when fragmentation prevents admission: e.g. if admission fails due to contig shortage, runtime can schedule a background defrag under tenant budget and return `ERR_EVICT_ENTERS_DEFRAG` so caller can retry after backoff.

alex: sounds good. i'll draft the PR with the API, config knobs, telemetry, and a short SDK retry recipe. will include sequence diagrams for admit -> token -> run -> preempt flow and an appendix of error codes.

deploy-bot: PR #4520 opened by alex: "evictor: tenant QoS, admission tokens, and cooperative preemption" — https://git.internal/redwood/pulls/4520 :eyes:

ben: i'll run perf harness against the branch. chris/maria/sara please review the admission semantics.

maria: one more thought — make compaction yield checkpoint cheap: persist small compacted ranges so preempted work does not fully roll back. follow-up RFC maybe.

alex: noted. thanks all — big win if this prevents noisy-neighbor p99 spikes. :party_parrot:
